page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-56 is a compute-focused instance powered by AMD EPYC 7B13 processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance allocates 56 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 28 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache layout provides 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. Instruction set support includes AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI extensions, though AVX-512 extensions are absent. Memory provision stands at 224 GB, delivering a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio that offers 4 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Benchmark testing highlights solid multi-core execution and in-memory throughput. In multi-threaded evaluation, the system achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 17030.0 and a stress-ng score of 82121.09, placing it in the top 25 percent of tested machines. Software compilation in Clang (42226.0) and ray tracing (62635.0) also showed strong results. PassMark testing returned a memory score of 3124.78 in the top ten percent, while Redis SET operations attained 61.92 million operations per second. In contrast, single-thread processing yielded median results, with Geekbench single-core scoring 1662.0 and uncached memory bandwidth testing reaching 137.27 GB/s for read and 68.92 GB/s for write.

The c2d-standard-56 does not include integrated local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned. Storage requirements must be met using external network-attached volumes, introducing potential I/O latency considerations depending on the selected storage tier. The high core count and ample memory allocation yield efficient resource density for CPU-heavy and memory-active workflows without paying for specialized accelerators. Best-fit workloads include CI/CD build environments, relational databases, in-memory caching systems, large-scale batch processing, and CPU-based inference workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-56 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 28 physical cores and 56 dedicated vCPUs alongside 224 GB of system memory, it maintains a balanced ratio of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring attached persistent storage for stateful deployments. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong multi-threaded capability, achieving top-tier memory scores in PassMark and strong results in stress-ng, Clang software compilation, and ray tracing. In-memory data workloads perform well, as evidenced by 61.92 million Redis SET operations per second and solid PassMark database metrics. Single-threaded metrics and large-block uncached memory bandwidth fall within median ranges. This hardware configuration is well suited for parallel build pipelines, high-concurrency web serving, relational and in-memory databases, and distributed batch processing.
